# Java 26.3 item integration fixtures

`item_integrations.json` contains normalized behavioral facts from the official
Java 26.3 server artifact, not expected values generated by VoxelCraft.
It intentionally covers a small first slice; it is not the full content catalogue.

- [Official launcher version metadata](https://piston-meta.mojang.com/v1/packages/702fe59163c6ee6578607daa85811d9bc9c7cc40/26.3.json).
- [Official server artifact](https://piston-data.mojang.com/v1/objects/33680f5f2ac32864d6d7cf5e56a705fdb3e05f4c/server.jar),
  SHA-1 `33680f5f2ac32864d6d7cf5e56a705fdb3e05f4c`.
- [Official release notes](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/48913133328013-Minecraft-Java-Edition-26-3).

The bundler contains `META-INF/versions/26.3/server-26.3.jar`. Fuel values come
from `data/minecraft/context_int_provider/cooking/time_*.json`, with item-to-fuel
associations checked in `net.minecraft.world.item.Items`. Normal fuel reduction
is 1 and fast cooking reduction is 2, using integer division. Notably the
selected version's dried-kelp provider is **4001 ticks**; rounding it to 4000
would lose reference precision. Crimson/warped planks have no cooking fuel.

Brewing and lead/saddle recipe facts identify their exact paths in the
artifact. The fixture keeps its original `pending_recipes` key so regenerated
output still diffs cleanly. The v0.7 content that registers leads and saddles
was merged in `22ad25c`, so these cases are now normal integration tests:
`retained_transport_recipes_match_java_26_3_and_consume_the_grid` crafts both
recipes and checks the grid is consumed.

The shared bucket scenarios in `tests/shared_buckets.rs` are original setups
based on Java 26.3 `BucketItem.use/emptyContents`, `BottleItem.use`,
`Player.mayUseItemAt`, `Bucketable.bucketMobPickup`, `BlockBehaviour.canBeReplaced`,
`ServerPlayerGameMode.useItemOn` and `ItemUtils.createFilledResult`. They cover
source pickup, pouring on the hit face (grass and ferns are not replaced in
place), water into a water-holding plant in place, destroying replaceable blocks
with their drops, creative item retention, stacked-container overflow, bottle
filling without source removal, Nether water evaporation, Adventure failure for
fluid buckets, and entity and block use taking priority over buckets on the CLI.
They also exercise VoxelCraft's existing creature payload and save format.
They do not establish full waterlogging, cauldron or offhand parity. VoxelCraft
has no separate dry/waterlogged block states.

Reproduce the data-derived facts from a downloaded server artifact:

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_item_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-item-integrations.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/item_integrations.json target/java-item-integrations.json
cargo test --release --test java_item_integrations --test shared_buckets
cargo test --release --no-default-features --test java_item_integrations --test shared_buckets
```

The extractor checks the exact artifact hash. Keep game binaries and inspection
output under ignored `target/`; only these normalized facts and original tests
belong in Git. Do not regenerate a new-version fixture over this version's file.

## Turtle equipment and potions

`turtle_integrations.json` records turtle helmet crafting/repair/equipment
stats and all normal/splash Turtle Master brewing variants. The reproducer
extracts recipes and repair tags from JSON and constants from the selected
server bytecode; it checks the known registration forms and fails on changes.
It does not read VoxelCraft source or the existing fixture.

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_turtle_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-turtle-integrations.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/turtle_integrations.json target/java-turtle-integrations.json
cargo test --release --test turtle_integrations --test process_persistence
cargo test --release --lib entity::potion::tests
```

The splash tests additionally use `ThrownSplashPotion.onHitAsPotion`,
`EntityTypes.SPLASH_POTION` (0.25 × 0.25 box) and
`ProjectileUtil.computeMargin` (0 through 0.3 based on flight ticks). Java 26.3
scales intensity by distance between collision boxes, not entity feet. Its
default duration scale is one. The narrow tests cover Turtle Master's two
effects, attenuation, the vertical query boundary and the existing instant
healing/harming path; they do not prove every projectile collision rule.

## Complete cooking-fuel registrations

`fuel_integrations.json` is extracted from all Items fuel registrations in
the pinned artifact, including nested property callbacks and colored
collections. It covers 347 registered fuels and 52 explicit non-fuel exceptions.
`tests/full_fuel_integrations.rs` checks every name implemented by VoxelCraft,
consumer/save behavior and integer rounding. Unregistered reference names remain
visible in `examples/fuel_inventory.rs` output; they are missing content rather
than completed integrations. See the [inventory evidence](../../../../docs/verification/2026-10-12-fuel-inventory.md).

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_fuel_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-fuel-integrations.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/fuel_integrations.json target/java-fuel-integrations.json
cargo run --release --no-default-features --example fuel_inventory > target/fuel-inventory.json
cargo test --release --test full_fuel_integrations
```

Since v0.12 the extractor names each item by its registry ID, not its `Items`
field (`java_item_associations.provider_ids`); the two fields that differ,
`DRY_SHORT_GRASS` and `DRY_TALL_GRASS`, are now `short_dry_grass` and
`tall_dry_grass`. The test and the inventory resolve Java IDs by ID or English
name (the block of coal is `coal_block`), and `only_java_fuels_burn` rejects
any VoxelCraft item that burns without being a Java fuel.

## Block mining properties

`block_mining.json` records every block `Blocks` registers (1,286): its
`destroyTime` (hardness), blast resistance and `requiresCorrectToolForDrops`,
plus the expanded `incorrect_for_<tier>_tool` tags and the sword and shears
`minesAndDrops` rule (cobweb only). `tools/java_block_properties.py` evaluates
`Blocks.<clinit>` bytecode on a small symbolic stack machine: `strength`,
`destroyTime`, `explosionResistance`, `instabreak`, `requiresCorrectToolForDrops`,
`ofFullCopy`/`ofLegacyCopy` of earlier blocks, helper methods, lambdas and the
colour and copper collections, with IDs from `BlockItemIds` and `BlockIds`.
Branches inside helpers run both ways and must agree; registrations inside a
branch, unknown opcodes and unknown collection helpers fail. The extractor also
checks `Player.hasCorrectToolForDrops`, `Tool.isCorrectForDrops` and the tool,
sword and shears rule order.

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_block_mining_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-block-mining.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/block_mining.json target/java-block-mining.json
cargo test --release --test java_block_mining --test shared_mining
```

`tests/java_block_mining.rs` maps every registered state to its Java block (by
ID, English name or an explicit state alias such as `lit furnace` or a bed
half), then compares hardness, `mining::can_harvest` and `mining::dig_progress`
for a bare hand, a stick, shears and all 35 tools against a model of Java's
rules built from this fixture, `mining.json` (mineable, sword and shears tags)
and `combat.json` (tier speeds). Air, water and lava are allow-listed: Java
never targets them. Blast resistance is recorded but VoxelCraft's explosions
don't model it yet.

## Composting

`compost.json` lists every compostable item (122) with its provider and chance,
from the `Items` `compostable` registrations (followed through callbacks and
colour collections, named by registry ID) and
`data/minecraft/context_int_provider/compostable/*.json`. Every provider is
checked to add the first layer to an empty composter, and
`ComposterBlock.addLayer` to roll the item's provider. It supersedes the
99-item hand-picked list in `plant_integrations.json`, which stays for its
existing tests.

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_compost_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-compost.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/compost.json target/java-compost.json
cargo test --release --test java_compost --test plant_integrations
```

## Anvil repair materials

`repair.json` lists every item with a `repairable` component (75) and its
material tag or item, with the tags expanded. `Items` sets the component
through tool forms (`ToolMaterial` repair tags), `humanoidArmor` and
`wolfArmor` (`ArmorMaterials`), or a direct `repairable` call (elytra, mace,
shield); horse and nautilus armor are checked to have none.
`tests/java_repair.rs` checks `enchant::repairs` for every registered
repairable item against every item as a candidate material, and that every
other item accepts no material.

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_repair_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-repair.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/repair.json target/java-repair.json
cargo test --release --test java_repair
```

## Registry names

`registry_names.json` lists every Java 26.3 block and item registry name with
its English display name, read from the official client
(SHA-1 `e877b6a07acd633fb3bb475002175cec036e7b87`): blockstate and item-model
file names, and `lang/en_us.json`. `examples/registry_audit.rs` reports the
names VoxelCraft doesn't register and the VoxelCraft names Java lacks. It is
a name-level probe, not a parity check. See the
[v0.12 audit](../../../../docs/verification/2026-10-23-v0.12-registry-audit.md).

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_registry_names.py /path/to/client.jar --output target/java-registry-names.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/registry_names.json target/java-registry-names.json
cargo run --release --no-default-features --example registry_audit > target/registry-audit.json
```

## Consumption durations

`consumption.json` records independent Java consumption timing for representative
food, dried kelp, milk and potion registrations. The reproducer verifies the
official server hash, default food/drink builders and their item associations;
unknown bytecode forms fail instead of inferring a duration from Rust.

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_consumption_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-consumption.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/consumption.json target/java-consumption.json
cargo test --release --test session_consumption --test process_persistence
```

It also pins the status effects and chance of the registered foods (spider eye,
poisonous potato, pufferfish, rotten flesh, raw chicken, golden apple, enchanted
golden apple) and the `alwaysEdible` set from `Foods`. The fixture proves these
facts, not complete food/effect parity: honey, chorus fruit and suspicious stew
are unregistered.

## Mining rules and ice support

`mining.json` records the expanded ice support tag, Silk Touch and dimension
rules, block interaction range, all Mining Fatigue amplifier factors and nine
explicit float-progress scenarios. The reproducer inspects official data and
bytecode, using reference operation order rather than Rust output.

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_mining_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-mining.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/mining.json target/java-mining.json
cargo test --release --test shared_mining --test process_persistence
```

This proves the stated rules and scenarios, not full block shapes, tool/effect
metadata or every Creative restriction. See the [mining evidence](../../../../docs/verification/2026-10-13-shared-mining.md).

## Gameplay lighting and spawning

`lighting_spawning.json` records reference biome lists, dimension rules,
floor/light checks, clock/weather cases and six independently modelled scene
families. The extractor checks official data and relevant bytecode forms; the
fixed-point scene model does not inspect Rust output.

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_lighting_spawning_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-lighting-spawning.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/lighting_spawning.json target/java-lighting-spawning.json
cargo test --release entity::monster_spawns::tests
cargo test --release --test lighting_persistence
```

These fixtures do not establish full shaped-block occlusion, category caps,
structure overrides or the complete roster. See the [lighting/spawning evidence](../../../../docs/verification/2026-10-13-lighting-spawning.md).

## Player melee

`combat.json` records the player's base attack attributes, entity interaction
ranges, every vanilla tool's attack-damage/speed modifiers with its tool-material
bonus, each tool material's durability, speed, enchantability and
incorrect-block/repair tags (with the incorrect tag's contents), the open-screen
range extras, and the constants `Player.attack` uses for attack strength,
criticals, sprint knockback, sweeps and exhaustion. The extractor reads `Items`,
`ToolMaterial`, `Attributes`, `Player`, `Container`, `ContainerEntity` and
`AbstractVillager` bytecode plus block tag data, and fails on unknown forms.

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_combat_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-combat.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/combat.json target/java-combat.json
cargo test --release --test shared_combat --test copper_tools --test shared_screen_ranges --test java_knockback
```

All 35 reference tools, including copper, are registered.

### Sweeping and knockback

`tools/extract_java_knockback_facts.py` (called by the combat extractor) adds the
sweep and knockback facts. Each is read from bytecode with the exact call and
constant sequence checked (`Player.attack`, `isSweepAttack`, `doSweepAttack`,
`attackVisualEffects`, `causeExtraKnockback`, `LivingEntity.knockback`,
`getKnockback`, `dealDefaultKnockback`, `hurtServer`, `Mob.doHurtTarget`,
`AbstractArrow.doKnockback`, `Projectile.calculateHorizontalHurtKnockbackDirection`,
`DamageSource.getSourcePosition`, `HoglinBase.throwTarget`, `Vec3.yRot`,
`Mth.sin/cos`, `Attributes`, `MobEffects`, the entity `createAttributes` of the
knockback-resistant mobs) and from the knockback, punch and sweeping-edge
enchantment data and the `swords` and `arrows` tags. The `cases` section holds
reference results (`knockback`, `attack_knockback`, `yaw_direction`,
`arrow_punch`, `hoglin_throw`, `sweep_eligibility`, `sweep_damage`, `sweep_reach`,
`attack_sounds`, `player_speed`) computed by a small model of Java's arithmetic
(float rounding where Java uses `float`) from the constants just extracted; they
are not generated from VoxelCraft. `tests/java_knockback.rs` checks the pure
rules against every case and then compares whole-game scenarios with an
evaluator built from the fixture's constants.

## Fishing loot

`fishing.json` records every entry of `gameplay/fishing` and its junk,
treasure and fish tables (weights, qualities, conditions, counts, damage
ranges and enchanting levels) plus the expanded `#on_random_loot` tag. The
extractor fails on unknown entry types, keys, conditions or loot functions and
checks the `LootPool.addRandomItem` positive-weight filter,
`SetItemDamageFunction` formula and `enchantItem` book conversion in bytecode.

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_fishing_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-fishing.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/fishing.json target/java-fishing.json
cargo test --release --test fishing_loot
```

The fixture proves table contents and the stated formulas. Loot uses
VoxelCraft's RNG, not Java's random sequence, so individual rolls are not
reproduced; the tests check shares and ranges.

`world_defects.json` extracts Nether spawn costs and structure loot pool
weights/counts/modifier names from the pinned server data, independently of
engine code. Reproduce with `tools/extract_java_world_defect_fixtures.py`.

## Recipes

`recipes.json` normalizes all 1,763 recipes in the pinned server's
`data/minecraft/recipe/*.json` (brewing, in `recipe/brewing/`, is a separate
system and not included): shaped patterns and keys, shapeless ingredient
lists, transmute, dye and imbue slots, cooking ingredient, result, time and
experience, stonecutting counts, smithing slots and the special recipes'
slots. Item tags stay by name in the recipes and are expanded once in
`item_tags`. A count of one is omitted. `cooking_speed` records 26.3's
furnace speed multiplier: every cooking recipe says 200 ticks, and
`AbstractFurnaceBlockEntity.getTotalCookTime` divides by the fuel's speed
(`context_float_provider/cooking/speed_default`), 2.0 in the
`predicate/block/fast_cooking` blocks (smoker and blast furnace), so they
take 100.

`tests/java_recipes.rs` compares both ways: every reference recipe whose
result and at least one alternative per slot are registered must exist with
the same shape (mirrors are equal), alternatives, count, cooking result,
experience and time, and its grids must craft it; every VoxelCraft crafting,
cooking, stonecutting and smithing recipe must have a Java counterpart.
Unregistered recipes are listed, not failed; intentional differences are in
the commented allow-lists in `tests/java_recipes/compare.rs`.
`examples/recipe_audit.rs` prints the same report, with the unregistered
recipes and the names they lack. See the
[recipe record](../../../../docs/verification/2026-10-27-v0.12-data-recipes.md).

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_recipe_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-recipes.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/recipes.json target/java-recipes.json
cargo test --release --test java_recipes
cargo run --release --no-default-features --example recipe_audit > target/recipe-audit.json
```

## Block loot

`block_loot.json` evaluates every block loot table in the pinned artifact
(`data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/*.json`, 1,201 tables) for all 1,286 Java
blocks. Wall variants (torches, signs, hanging signs, banners, heads and coral
fans, 63 in all) take their standing block's table through `Blocks.wallVariant`;
the 22 other blocks without a table (air, fluids, portals, bedrock, command and
structure blocks and the like) drop nothing. For every combination of the
block-state values a table's conditions name (`*` for any other value) and
for each mining scenario (bare hand, a plain pickaxe, shears, Silk Touch,
Fortune I-III) it stores each item's exact chance, count range, mean and
variance. The extractor models `set_count`, `limit_count`, the three Fortune
formulas, `table_bonus` and `random_chance` after checking their bytecode,
and fails on any entry type, condition, function or key it doesn't know.
Mining has no explosion, so `survives_explosion` passes and `explosion_decay`
keeps every item. A separate `explosion` scenario evaluates each table as
`ServerExplosion.interactWithBlocks` does with decay at radius 4 (a TNT
block or creeper): an empty tool, `survives_explosion` passing with chance
1/4 (`ExplosionCondition`) and each item surviving `explosion_decay` with
chance 1/4 (`ApplyExplosionDecay`), both checked in bytecode. A decorated pot broken by a `#breaks_decorated_pots` tool without
Silk Touch is cracked first (`DecoratedPotBlock.playerWillDestroy`) and drops
its four sides, bricks when undecorated.

`tests/java_block_loot.rs` maps every registered VoxelCraft state to its Java
block and state values, breaks it through `World::spill_with_item` with each
scenario's tool that can harvest it (and through `World::spill_exploded` for
the explosion scenario, whatever the block needs), and compares the drops: exactly for fixed
drops, and by chance and mean (five standard errors, seeded world RNG) for
random ones. It also breaks beds and double tall grass and large ferns through
the mining session, where Java drops the loot once. Unregistered Java blocks are
listed, not failed; `examples/block_loot_audit.rs` prints them with the counts.
See the [verification record](../../../../docs/verification/2026-10-27-v0.12-data-drops.md).

```sh
python3 tools/extract_java_block_loot_fixtures.py /path/to/server.jar --output target/java-block-loot.json
diff tests/fixtures/java/26.3/block_loot.json target/java-block-loot.json
cargo test --release --test java_block_loot
cargo run --release --no-default-features --example block_loot_audit > target/block-loot-audit.json
```
